Random Act of Kindness

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we look at how South Africans are trying to make a difference, one small act of kindness at a time.

Summary:
It started as a Nek nomination, film yourself drinking a pint of alcohol within 24 hours and nominate a friend or two, but Brent Lindeque decided to make a difference. Instead of taking a drink, he decided to buy a meal for a beggar and film the whole process. Within hours of putting his short video online, thousands of people had watched his clip and started filming themselves showing someone else a random act of kindness.

Thousands of videos have since been put online from all over the world and now a year later, Brent and a few of his friends want to continue the campaign, to get South Africans to show each other random acts of kindness.

Further information:
Sunday, 1 February marks the one year anniversary since Brent's original video went viral which is why this Sunday was most ideal.

Press Release:


Random Acts of Kindness

No one could have foreseen that a popular online campaign to drink alcohol and nominate friends to do the same, would snowball into a global phenomenon inspiring random acts of kindness – or RAK – to be filmed and posted online. Carte Blanche kicks-off the RAK 2015 drive as we take up the challenge.

Producer: Chwayitisa Futshane


Script:


VO: It originated from the so called Neknominations drinking game.
Drink a pint of alcohol, on camera, and then nominate a friend to do the same.

VO: But when Brent Lindeque, who now presents a Good News show on Cliff Central, received his Neknomination, he made a decision that would get the world involved in a very different way.


UPSOUND Brent: I got nominated and instead of downing a drink, I decided to feed a homeless man and in that the Neknomination became the RAK nomination which is a random act of kindness

VO: Brent’s act of kindness showed that the spirit of Ubuntu is still truly alive in South Africa, so much so, that within hours, his video had gone viral.

Thousands of people from around the world watched his video and started uploading their own versions of Random acts of kindness.

UPSOUND Brent: My hope was that my two friends would nominate their two friends and it would grow to maybe a circle of ten people that would help and feed our fellow South Africans.

VO: But it just kept growing as more and more people uploaded their videos.

From Johannesburg….. to Edinburgh… to Harare.


UPSOUND Brent: People were emailing me on a daily basis with all the amazing stuff that they were doing.
There was a South African guy based in London, who, it was very cold at the time. He walked out of a store, gave a homeless man a hot shot chocolate and a meal, and then asked him to hold the camera. While he ws holding the camera, he took off one of his winter jackets, that his father had given him, gave him the jacket and left him with some food in the jacket as well.

VO: This year, Brent and a few of his friends are ready to take the campaign he started a year ago, to the next level.


Andrew Ross, one of the key organizers of RAK 15, explained their vision.


03:19:37
The plan for 2015 obviously kicks off with Brents launch video. The 2014 video was literally random, it was spontanteous. We’ve tried deliberately not to replicate that so we went to an orphanage in Soweto where all they need is love.


VO: RAK15 and Carte Blanche hope that this new video will encourage even more South Africans to show each other a bit of kindness.

UPSOUND Brent: There are so many simple ways, it’s not just about feeding the whole of South Africa, there’s simple things that you could do to do a random act of kindness.
VO: And giving each other a helping hand, is where all South Africans can make a difference.
Brent: That’s what matters. The video is not about me, it’s not about you, it’s about South Africa, it’s about the world caring for each other.
